title: Console Surface Spectrum Harmonizer: Brand-Adaptive Theming for Dark Mode
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design a deterministic mapping layer that harmonizes brand color palettes and high-contrast accessibility needs with the console surface system in dark mode. The Surface Spectrum Harmonizer provides a translation and fallback engine (design-level spec + token naming conventions) so that: 1) brand accents retain perceived hue and vibrance across surface elevations; 2) interactive components (buttons, tables, inputs, dropdowns) remain distinguishable and meet WCAG AA for normal text and 3:1 for UI components where required; 3) charts and data visualizations maintain categorical separability while avoiding saturation clashes with surface tones.

Background: We currently have multiple ad-hoc brand overrides and manual component tweaks that cause inconsistencies during private deployments and Dedicated installs where customers push custom brand tokens. This ticket defines a composable, documented mapping strategy rather than per-component patches.

Design deliverables & approach:
- Token model: introduce a small set of derived tokens (surface-base, surface-muted, surface-elev-1..4, accent-solid, accent-muted, interactive-state-primary, interactive-state-hover, outline-strong) and a spectrum translation function called "harmonize()" that specifies hue preservation with contrast-preserving luminance shifts and optional desaturation for deep-dark surfaces.
- Naming: add token prefixes --rh-spectrum-*, with clear fallbacks for missing brand tokens (rh-spectrum-fallback-<role>).
- Component overrides: document exact overrides for Primary/Secondary/Destructive buttons (elevation overlay, border emphasis, text emphasis ratios), table row and divider treatments for zebra/compact modes, and chart palette generators that reserve up to 4 high-contrast accent slots before going to soft-muted variations.
- Contrast targets: default normal text >= 4.5:1, button text >= 4.5:1, icon-only controls >= 3:1, decorative chart elements may be lower but primary data marks >= 4.5:1.
- Edge cases: very saturated brand colors (neon greens/pinks) will be passed through a controlled desaturation step + overlay blend to avoid visual vibration on 10–15% of iconography. The spec includes an algorithmic example and a compact reference table for designers and engineering.

Implementation notes for handoff:
- Provide CSS var map and pseudo-code for harmonize() (HSL-based adjustments then perceptual luminance checks). Engineers: use kerma/oklab helpers in runtime for better perceptual matching.
- Migration: create opt-in feature flag (theme.harmonizer=v1) so rolling updates are possible. Start with canary in internal account and one customer with custom brand tokens.
- Testing: include a visual diff checklist (Figma frames for 6 canonical pages: dashboard, chat, model-run view, cost analytics, alerts table, onboarding) and automated storybook screenshots across 8 brand palettes.

Success criteria:
- All canonical pages in canary show no contrast regressions vs current baseline; primary interactive components meet contrast targets; charts retain category separability in 85% of customer brand palettes tested.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Do we run the harmonize function at build time (static token generation) or at runtime in the console (dynamic per-tenant)? Proposal: start static during theme compilation for Hosted + Dedicated, evaluate runtime for Private if customers require dynamic on-the-fly branding.
- How aggressive should desaturation be for extreme brand hues? Default conservative with an opt-in aggressive mode for customers who prefer color fidelity over strict contrast.

Next steps:
1) Sync with engineering runtime owners to land variables and pseudo-code (ENG-20198). 2) Produce Figma kit with harmonizer variants for 8 brand palettes (link below). 3) Author storybook tests and an internal canary rollout plan.
